## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Minecraft-inspired game in the existing project.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finishing.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (maximum 1280px wide) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained browser game named Blockbound using HTML Canvas, with an isometric voxel-style world and no external game dependencies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with a generated block world, player movement and hopping, mining and block placement, inventory hotbar, rotating/zoomable camera, objectives, and mobile touch controls.
- Started a local server and opened the game in Playwright; browser reported only a missing `favicon.ico` (404).
- Installed Chromium for Playwright after the initial browser launch failed because it was not installed.
- Fixed block mining/terrain height handling and corrected target selection to match the camera-facing direction.

### Active
- Verify gameplay and visuals, including inspecting a compliant JPEG screenshot.
- Check browser console and game interactions for remaining issues.

### Blocked
- Screenshot capture through `playwright-cli screenshot` timed out while waiting for fonts; a `run-code` capture wrote `screenshots/world.jpg`, but its byte-array output was truncated and the image has not been inspected.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest `screenshots/world.jpg` and verify the rendered scene at a viewport no wider than 1280px.
2. Exercise start, movement, mining, placement, hotbar, and reset; fix any issues found.
3. Summarize the finished game and briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: entire playable game implementation and UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project currently contains untracked files including `index.html`.
- Local server was launched with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright browser is open at `http://localhost:3002`; screenshot output requested at `screenshots/world.jpg`.
